virtual_junction.label: REPORTED, NOT GATED (D0020 item 2): die-average Tj ('virtual junction temperature'), NOT the registered criterion (O003's Tj is the maximum nodal value on the die top face, three-level gci_capped, D0013); it decides nothing
virtual_junction.definition: per die and thermal level: T_vj = (1/A) * integral over the die top face of T_h dA, the area-weighted mean of the scikit-fem solution T_h over the die's top face (the heat-source face, area A = the die footprint), as thermal_fem.solve computes ThermalResult.tj_mean: the facet load vector of the top face (FacetBasis, intorder 4) restricted to the face DOFs, divided by its sum A (checked against the footprint area to 1e-6), dotted with the nodal temperatures; the method of T0325's tj_osc.py.  Per die: GCI_vj = mfos.metrics.gci_capped(T_vj levels 0, 1, 2, floor 1e-3 K); per layout: mfos.metrics.tj_bounds on T_vj

band_step.note: T0332, REPORTED, NOT GATED: the die-average best is the layout A1's formula (mfos.metrics.headroom_per_reference, unchanged) picks when T_vj replaces Tj max (virtual_junction_report's row copy).  If the gated rows lack its band columns, its BAND em_jobs are submitted through its reference's main Driver and the run's Scheduler (same job keys and solver settings, so a resumed run finds them) after every gated solve is done, and their values go into the report's row copy only.  A failure, a phase stop or --replay-only leaves h_lo_vj null with a reason
